newsitem.title: USA: Columbia says to cooperate with government.
newsitem.headline: Columbia says to cooperate with government.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp said Wednesday it intends to cooperate fully with the government and takes very seriously allegations made against three of its employees.
The company said it understands that attorneys for the employees, indicted on charges of fraud Wednesday, will meet with the government to discuss the indictments.
"I can assure you that we take these allegations very seriously and will cooperate fully with the government," said Dr. Thomas Frist, chairman and chief executive of Columbia, in a statement.
Columbia said it has learned that the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida, in Fort Myers, issued an indictment against three Columbia employees.
"The indictment relates to Medicare and CHAMPUS reimbursement issues since 1986 at Columbia Fawcett Memorial Hospital, a Port Charlotte, Fla. hospital acquired by Columbia in 1992," the company said.
"The specific allegations relate to alleged false characterization of interest payments on certain debt resulting in overpayments to the hospital by Medicare and CHAMPUS," the company said.
CHAMPUS, or the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Uniformed Services, is the U.S. military's equivalent of the Medicare program.
